subject: Recap: Redwood integration discussion & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Redwood integration discussion & next steps

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciated the candid run-through of Acme's priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Key pain points and goals (as I understood them):
- Latency variability on your chat endpoint, especially during peak traffic; you need consistent 95th percentile latency < 200ms.
- High unit cost for embedding/reranking pipeline at your search scale — looking to cut per-query token cost and speed up nearest-neighbor lookups.
- Need structured outputs from model calls (JSON/schema enforcement) to reduce downstream parsing fragility.
- Desire for streaming/token-level responses for live UX, and function-calling integration for deterministic actions (e.g., update internal ticket).
- Data residency concern — you asked about Private/VPC options for production PII workloads.

Product fit summary:
- Redwood streaming + function-calling can replace your current ad-hoc polling and reduce latency for interactive chat.
- Embeddings + reranker flow: we recommend co-locating the embedding stage on dedicated capacity and using our prefix-caching + approximate nearest neighbor support to reduce compute and latency.
- SDK changes: our client (v2.3) supports streaming with early flush, structured output enforcement via schema helpers, and built-in reranking utilities. I attached a short integration guide that covers the code snippets we discussed.

Action items / next steps:
1) I’ll share the SDK integration guide, a draft SOW, and the demo recording (attached).
2) Technical deep-dive with your platform/infra team — suggested participants: Dev (your platform engineer), Sofia (platform), our Dev Patel + Rishi.
3) Discuss Private/VPC options and security questionnaire in that call; Rishi will lead on compliance details.
4) We can provide a short PoC (30–60 days): sandbox tokens, telemetry, and a small reserved capacity bump for consistent latency.

Proposed times for the technical call (PT): Tue May 11 at 10am or 2pm — let me know what works.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf; SOW-draft-Acme-Redwood.pdf; redwood-demo-recording.mp4 (link stub)

Thanks — I’ll coordinate calendar once you confirm a slot.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Amit Shah <amit@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Lopez <s.lopez@acme.com>, platform@acme.com, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Redwood integration discussion & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. This looks right to me. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Prioritization: our immediate goal is to stabilize chat latency (95th pctl) — the embedding cost/re-ranking is next in priority but still important for our search relevance SLA.
- For the PoC we’d like to validate both streaming chat UX and a sample reranker for our top 1,000 queries. If the PoC shows >30% cost reduction on embeddings and 20% improvement in reranked CTR, we’ll be ready to move to a reserved capacity conversation.
- Data residency: for PII-bearing chat logs, we’ll need Private/VPC or a firm guarantee around data at rest. Please have Rishi/your security lead prepare the data flow and retention notes.

Sofia and our platform team will join the tech call. Tue May 11 at 10am PT works for us — please send invite.

Thanks, looking forward to the deep-dive.

Great — I’ve scheduled the technical deep-dive for Tue May 11 at 10:00 AM PT and sent the calendar invite to the group.

Agenda (30–45 min):
- 10 min: PoC goals & success metrics (Marissa + Amit)
- 10 min: Architecture & network/data residency questions (Rishi + Dev)
- 10 min: SDK integration walkthrough (Dev Patel) — streaming, function-calling, structured outputs, embeddings/reranking snippets
- 5–10 min: SOW & timeline discussion (Marissa)

Rishi will follow up after the call with a short security/data-residency note and a checklist for SOC2/data-flow items. I’ll also drop the PoC plan and acceptance criteria in the HubSpot deal record: https://hubspot.example/deal/ACME-2027-005.

If anything changes on your side, let me know and I’ll update the invite. Looking forward to the call.

_thread_summary: Post-call sales recap for Acme covering latency, embeddings/reranking, streaming, function calling, structured outputs, and Private/VPC. Agreed to technical deep-dive May 11 and PoC scope; attachments and SOW shared.
